question: Does the still-documented Google Drive API v2 expose a strong file ETag and atomically reject a metadata update that reuses that ETag after an intervening successful update?
kind: Explicitly authorized, bounded capability probe on one file previously created and retained by Cirrove's isolated Google write validator.
authorization: On 2026-09-20 the owner asked Cirrove to test the proposed Drive v2 ETag path to get a quick evidence-based answer. The earlier Google write authorization already limits mutations to run-owned validation objects.
scope: The exact multipart file whose prepared identity, upload receipt and SHA-256 readback were recorded by the completed fifth Google create-validation run. The ordinary mounted Google account and every pre-existing user item are excluded.
arms: GET the exact file through Drive v2 and require a syntactically strong file-resource ETag before any mutation.
PATCH the exact file's title with If-Match set to that current ETag.
PATCH another title while deliberately reusing the now-stale ETag.
GET the exact identity again and restore its original title with the current ETag.
prediction: Drive v2 will return a strong ETag, accept the first conditional rename, reject the stale rename with HTTP 412, and accept the conditional restoration. This would establish a viable metadata compare-and-set primitive for a hybrid v3-read/v2-write adapter, not yet content replacement or mounted-write reliability.
endpoint: Success requires all four observations and the original name restored. No ETag stops before mutation. An accepted stale request is a hard failure but is still followed by an exact re-read and conditional restoration. Any unexpected identity, parent, name or version stops without overwriting it.
decision_rule: Only a real strong v2 ETag plus a 412 for its stale reuse permits further conditional Google write work. The v2 token must never be inferred from Drive's numeric version. Ordinary Google mounts remain read-only regardless of this single result.

synthetic_precheck.coverage: Current ETag accepted, stale ETag rejected, original name restored; missing ETag performs no mutation.

result.interpretation: Drive v2 supplied a usable strong file-resource ETag and enforced it atomically for metadata PATCH on this retained app-created binary file. This closes the metadata compare-and-set question for this account and operation. It does not yet prove conditional content upload, trash/delete, shared-drive behavior, long-session reliability or a writable mount.
